policy: This audit never fabricates approval. Every item below remains PENDING_USER_DECISION until the user explicitly approves it.

items.title: Untrusted engine asset import scope
items.meaning: Whether the release candidate may claim that imported third-party engine assets were validated at import time.
existing_evidence: Phase 8 recorded performed=false for engine asset import.
Phase 9 re-verified performed=false; no Unity/Blender import ran.
Asset download paths now reject traversal, stream and device names.
License records and provenance are captured, but import-time content validation (scripts, shaders, prefabs) is not implemented.
items.remaining_risk: An asset that passes path validation may still contain malicious or incompatible engine content. Enabling automated import without a separate review would widen the trust boundary.
conditions: Keep automated import disabled for this release candidate.
Require a separate human-approved import test before enabling it.
Do not describe downloaded assets as engine-verified.
consequences_if_accepted: Release candidate remains honest about unverified import.
consequences_if_rejected: The release candidate must block all asset download features, not only import, or add import-time validation before release.

items.title: No-live-provider decision
items.meaning: Whether the release candidate is acceptable without any successful live AI provider request, and whether live content handling is trusted as data-only.
existing_evidence: Phase 7 recorded one approved live attempt that failed; live model quality is unmeasured.
Phase 9 made zero provider requests and read no credentials.
Provider routing, quota and paid-fallback policies pass offline tests.
Response validation marks untrusted input and the reasoning prompt treats target content as data.
items.remaining_risk: Live connectivity, provider terms, model quality, latency and prompt-injection behaviour are unverified. Offline fixtures cannot prove live behaviour.
conditions: Keep the no-live-provider rule in force for this release candidate.
Do not claim live AI works or that model output was verified.
Authorize any future live request separately, per request.
consequences_if_accepted: Release candidate is an offline-verified build with AI unavailable unless a later human-approved live test succeeds.
consequences_if_rejected: A separately approved live validation must be completed before the release candidate can advance.

items.title: DNS resolver resource accumulation
items.meaning: Whether a fixed-size resolver pool with fast capacity failure is acceptable given that getaddrinfo itself cannot be cancelled.
existing_evidence: Phase 8 used one daemon thread per lookup; repeated hung lookups could accumulate threads.
Phase 9 replaced this with a fixed pool of at most 4 daemon workers.
New offline tests prove success, failure, timeout, capacity exhaustion, worker reclamation, idle shutdown and honest reporting of hung workers.
The audit does not claim OS-level termination of a hung getaddrinfo.
items.remaining_risk: Four permanently hung OS resolver calls would occupy the whole pool, after which new DNS requests fail fast. This is bounded but still a denial-of-DNS condition until the OS resolver returns or the process restarts.
conditions: Document the residual denial-of-DNS condition in release notes.
Revisit process-isolated resolution only if observation shows repeated capacity exhaustion.
consequences_if_accepted: No unbounded thread growth; degradation is explicit and testable.
consequences_if_rejected: A separately terminable resolver process must be built and proven before release, which adds subprocess lifecycle risk.

recommended_combined_outcome: Accept S12 with import disabled, accept S14 as offline-only, and accept R3 as bounded mitigation with monitoring.
